Legendary Traders: Warren Buffett

Started investing at 11. Built Berkshire Hathaway from a failing textile mill into one of the largest companies on Earth. Never chased hype - bought wonderful businesses at fair prices and held them for decades.

His most famous line still holds up: be fearful when others are greedy, and greedy when others are fearful.

Not financial advice - educational content only.

#warrenbuffett #investing #stockmarket #valueinvesting #berkshirehathaway #financeeducation #legendarytraders #wallstreet #quantcodeai

Legendary Traders: Jesse Livermore

Started trading in the early 1900s with almost nothing and became known as the "boy plunger" for making and losing several fortunes. Famously shorted the market before the 1929 crash - and still went broke more than once breaking his own rules.

His real lesson wasn't a strategy. It was discipline.

Not financial advice - educational content only.

#jesselivermore #legendarytraders #investing #stockmarket #tradingpsychology #financeeducation #wallstreet #quantcodeai

Legendary Traders: Jim Simons

A mathematician before he ever traded a stock. In 1988 he started the Medallion Fund and used math and computer models instead of gut instinct - returning about 66% a year before fees for over three decades, a track record almost nobody else in history has matched.

He hired physicists and codebreakers instead of traditional Wall Street traders. Disciplined data beat intuition, again and again.

Not financial advice - educational content only.

#jimsimons #legendarytraders #quant #investing #stockmarket #financeeducation #wallstreet #quantcodeai

4 investing myths that just will not die:

You don't need a lot of money to start. Stocks don't always go up. Day trading rarely beats simple index investing. And checking your portfolio daily usually makes decisions worse, not better.

Slow down, zoom out.

Not financial advice - educational content only.

#investingmyths #investing #stockmarket #financeeducation #stocks #investingtips #personalfinance #wallstreet #quantcodeai

Legendary Traders: Peter Lynch

Ran Fidelity's Magellan Fund from 1977 to 1990 and averaged about 29% a year, growing it from roughly $20 million to more than $14 billion - the best-performing mutual fund in the world at the time.

His edge wasn't a secret formula. It was paying attention to the businesses and products already around him, and having the patience to let a good idea compound.

Not financial advice - educational content only.

#peterlynch #legendarytraders #investing #stockmarket #magellanfund #financeeducation #wallstreet #quantcodeai

4 more investing myths that just will not die:

A high dividend yield isn't automatically safer. Owning 20 stocks in one sector isn't real diversification. Trying to dodge the market's worst days often means missing its best ones too. And a fund's past performance rarely predicts its future.

Evidence over instinct.

Not financial advice - educational content only.

#investingmyths #investing #stockmarket #financeeducation #stocks #investingtips #personalfinance #wallstreet #quantcodeai

Legendary Traders: Ray Dalio

Started Bridgewater Associates in 1975, at just 26, out of a two bedroom apartment in Manhattan. Today it's the largest hedge fund in the world.

His edge was radical transparency - recording meetings and openly rating employees so bad ideas got challenged by anyone in the room. He's also known for the All Weather portfolio, built to hold up in any economic climate.

Not financial advice - educational content only.

#raydalio #legendarytraders #bridgewater #investing #stockmarket #financeeducation #wallstreet #quantcodeai

Stock or Not: guess which one is riskier.

Stock A: PE of 27.9x. Stock B: PE of 18.3x. Which one is the riskier growth stock?

Stock A is NVIDIA - revenue up 106% this year. Stock B is Johnson & Johnson, growing single digits. NVIDIA's PE looks high, but its PEG ratio is just 0.63 - actually cheap once you adjust for growth.

The number alone never tells the whole story.

Not financial advice - educational content only.

#stockmarket #investing #nvidia #financeeducation #stockquiz #wallstreet #quantcodeai

Guess the company from 3 facts:

1) Profit margin of just 3% - one of the thinnest in retail.
2) PEG ratio of 4.5x - pricier than almost any other 'boring' stock.
3) Earnings grew 45% year over year.

It's Costco. Investors pay a premium for a wafer-thin margin business, because the membership model is that reliable.

Not financial advice - educational content only.

#costco #stockmarket #investing #financeeducation #guessthecompany #wallstreet #quantcodeai

Rate My Portfolio: a common beginner mistake we made up to illustrate the point (not a real submission).

90% in one AI stock. 10% in cash. That's it - no bonds, no other sectors, nothing international.

Red flag #1: zero diversification - one bad earnings report and the whole thing moves together.
Red flag #2: no real cash cushion for when an actual buying opportunity shows up.

This isn't a portfolio, it's a single bet wearing a costume.

Not financial advice - educational content only.

#ratemyportfolio #investing #stockmarket #financeeducation #personalfinance #wallstreet #quantcodeai
